questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem drive at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: Highways and roads freeze before ramps and bridges.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Ramps and bridges are in the air, so they freeze faster than regular roads in cold weather. Drive slowly and carefully when crossing a bridge in freezing temperatures.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.
A blasting zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What do round signs indicate?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Upcoming railroad crossings.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn drivers of an upcoming railroad crossing. Be extra careful when you see this sign.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep roads safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are permitted on an upcoming narrow bridge.
The bridge ahead is open to one-way traffic only.
The bridge ahead is wide enough for only one car at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that an upcoming bridge is too narrow to pass a truck. Drive carefully.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right, not a privilege.
Privilege, not a right.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege that you must earn and keep.

questions.question: A vehicle's stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your own reaction time.
The time of day.
The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
The condition and type of your vehicle's tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather and visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: When driving through a curve, the most important thing to do is:

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part of the curve.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Accelerate gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the posted speed limit before, throughout, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve to keep control of your vehicle. Your vehicle may be hard to turn because of inertia.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: Passing is not permitted.
Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you can pass on the left if there is no oncoming traffic. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: You come to a complete stop at an intersection. You yield to traffic and pedestrians. Then you go when it is safe. What traffic light means this?

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do if there are two railroad tracks next to each other?

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
When one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: When there are two tracks side by side, a second train might come on the other track. Wait until you are sure no train is coming from either direction on either track before you cross.

questions.question: You are driving on an interstate. Traffic is merging from on-ramps on your right. What is the best thing to do?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Maintain your speed and position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: When you see an on-ramp ahead, move to the left lane when it is safe. This gives vehicles room to enter the highway from the right.

questions.question: You turn left onto a one-way street. Which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to your previous lane.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you came from.

questions.question: You park your car downhill on a two-way street. Which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parked downhill, turn your wheels toward the side of the road. If your car rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: When can you NOT cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is disabled.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you do it safely and do not get in the way of other traffic.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks does your body process in one hour?

options.text: Three alcoholic drinks an hour.
One alcoholic drink an hour.
Two alcoholic drinks an hour.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One alcoholic drink an hour.
questions.explanation: Your body processes about one drink per hour. But many things affect how impaired you become, like how much you drink, how fast you drink it, your weight, if you have eaten, and your health.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: Are following a small passenger vehicle.
Are being tailgated by another driver.
Are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are being tailgated by another driver.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, add more space in front of your car. Slow down gradually or change lanes. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: Your car starts to skid. Which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the wheel in the direction you want the car to go. When the car starts to straighten, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in bad weather?

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, do not slam on the brakes or make sharp, quick turns. Smooth steering and braking help you keep control of your car.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly so you can stop within the light of your headlights.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep your instrument panel lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly so you can stop within the light of your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop your vehicle within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: You arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles on your right and left. What should you do?

options.text: Let the vehicle on your left go first.
Let the vehicle on your right go first.
Wait until all vehicles leave before you proceed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When multiple vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Drivers then proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after rain.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery during the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. This happens because rain pushes oil from the asphalt to the road surface. Hot weather makes this worse because heat and water together cause more oil to rise to the surface.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep scanning the road for possible hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep scanning the road for possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead for potential hazards. Do not stare only at the road right in front of your car. Scan ahead and stay alert to vehicles around you.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and then:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgating cars.
Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you than vehicles from the right. Then look right, then look left again to check for any vehicles you may have missed.
